chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: "There is no pre-emptive right (shuf'ah) for the Jews and the Christians." And he said: "There is no pre-emptive right except for a partner who is not a co-heir."
He said: "And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The guardian of the orphan is in the position of his father; he takes the pre-emptive right for him if he has a desire for it.'"
And he said: "There is a pre-emptive right for the absent one."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: Pre-emptive right (the right of a co-owner or partner to buy out the share of another before it is sold to a third party)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of pre-emption (*shuf'ah*) by excluding People of the Book and limiting it to non-co-heir partners, while elevating the orphan's guardian to the status of a father for this right. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on protecting property rights within specific kinship and partnership bonds, ensuring that the right is exercised by those with a genuine interest rather than mere proximity. The inclusion of the absent party's right underscores the procedural fairness inherent in Islamic property law.
